title: Affine supported perfect zero detector
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], equipped with derived localizations for its module sheaves and their open restrictions [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $s$ be a finite set of affine opens covering $X$ with $|s|\leq 1$. Let $T\subseteq X$ be closed with quasi-compact complement. There exists a perfect quasi-coherent derived object $E$ [def-pc-perfect-complex] whose cohomology stalks vanish outside $T$, such that, for every quasi-coherent derived object $K$ supported on $T$, vanishing of $\operatorname{Hom}(E[n],K)$ for all $n\in\mathbf Z$ implies that $K$ is zero.

proof.text: If the cover is empty, its union is empty, so X has no points. Every module sheaf and every derived object is zero. Take the strictly perfect zero complex. Otherwise the cover has one member, which equals X. Thus X is affine. Identify X with Spec A by the canonical affine presentation. Quasi-compactness of X minus T gives finitely many functions f_i whose principal opens cover that complement. Sheafify the actual finite Koszul complex on these functions and localize it. It is perfect and has quasi-coherent cohomology. Each f_i acts null-homotopically, so its cohomology stalks vanish off their common zero locus T (Tag 0663). For a quasi-coherent K supported on T and orthogonal to every shift of this complex, apply koszul_open_orthogonality with the affine chart equal to X and open X minus T. The restriction of K to this open is zero: its cohomology sheaves have zero stalks there. The canonical unit therefore identifies K with derived pushforward of zero. A right adjoint preserves zero, so K is zero. The same calculation handles T empty (the Koszul complex is acyclic) and T equal to X (the empty Koszul tuple).

For triangulated closure the source has DerivedCategory.homologyProperty_isTriangulated, which additionally needs weak Serre class instances; these are not supplied for the supported quasi-coherent property. Existing KoszulOpenOrthogonality supplies the orthogonality input, not the finite supported perfect object construction. lean.statement:
theorem supported_perfect_detector_affine
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (s : Finset X.affineOpens) (hcover : (⨆ U ∈ s, (U : X.Opens)) = ⊤)
    (hcard : s.card ≤ 1) (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T) (hTc : IsCompact Tᶜ) :
    ∃ E : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X, Scheme.IsPerfect X E.obj ∧
      (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : X), x ∉ T →
        Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj E.obj).val.presheaf x))) ∧
      ∀ K : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X,
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : X), x ∉ T →
          Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj K.obj).val.presheaf x))) →
        (∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton (E.obj⟦n⟧ ⟶ K.obj)) → IsZero K.obj
